paper.citation: P. Barrios Hita, A. Trushechkin, H. Kampermann, M. Epping, D. Bruß, Quantum Mechanics Based on Real Numbers: A Consistent Description, Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202 (2026)

phases: the composition postulate is split off the real-QM model node
the new real-number model is identified with complex quantum theory
the no-go route of Renou et al. is kept and given its premises explicitly

nodes.label: Postulate (iv): Kronecker composition (Renou et al.)
nodes.def: H_ST = H_S ⊗ H_T (tensor product over the field of the theory); local operators act as A ⊗ 1; independent preparations are tensor products.

nodes.label: Postulate (P4): local action (Barrios Hita et al.)
nodes.def: There are embeddings ξ (independent preparation) and η^i (local operation) with η^1(A)ξ(ψ1,ψ2) = ξ(Aψ1,ψ2) and η^2(B)ξ(ψ1,ψ2) = ξ(ψ1,Bψ2)  (Eq. (75)).

nodes.label: Realification maps S, T, R (real-number QM)
nodes.def: S(ψ) = Re ψ ⊗|0> + Im ψ ⊗|1>;  T(A) = Re A ⊗ 1 + Im A ⊗ J;  R(Ψ) = Re Ψ ⊗ ψ_even^(N) + Im Ψ ⊗ ψ_odd^(N);  T on N flags uses I^(N), J^(N).

nodes.label: Real-number QM with the flag tensor product ⊗_F
nodes.def: Postulates (P1)–(P3) over R and (P4): states are classes in R^{2dA}⊗R^{2dB} / ker; canonical representatives lie in the range of P = (1 − J_A⊗J_B)/2; observables are T(A) (commute with J).

nodes.label: Real state space R^d ⊗ R²_F (real-number QM)
nodes.def: Vectors S(ψ) ∈ R^{2d}; the phase orbit {(1⊗R(α))S(ψ)} is one physical state; density operator T(ρ)/2.

nodes.label: Canonical flag subspace (real-number QM, N parties)
nodes.def: span{ψ_even^(N), ψ_odd^(N)} ⊂ (R²)^{⊗N}: the subspace on which all local J_k coincide.

nodes.label: States of two independent sources (network scenario)
nodes.def: Renou et al.: Σ_λ P(λ) σ^λ_{AB1} ⊗ σ^λ_{B2C} with real σ. Flag model: R(Ψ_{AB1} ⊗ Ψ_{B2C}).

nodes.label: Outcome probabilities P(a,b,c|x,z) (network scenario)
nodes.def: Born rule (iii)/(P3) for the three-party entanglement-swapping experiment.

nodes.label: Network correlations with T > 7.6605 (network scenario)
nodes.def: Statistics of the entanglement-swapping experiment whose T exceeds the bound for real QM with postulate (iv).
nodes.glue: GEN_GPT_Level v2.6: target of edge D6 (currently e-bell)

nodes.label: Experimental discrimination of a real-number theory from complex QT
nodes.def: Existence of an experiment whose statistics differ between the two theories.

edges.statement: T: M_d(C) → M_2d(R) is an injective unital real-algebra homomorphism with T(A†) = T(A)^T, and its image is the commutant of Jd = 1⊗J.
edges.check: block-matrix identities with d x d matrix symbols (d symbolic): all hold

edges.statement: S is real-linear and bijective C^d → R^2d with T(A)S(ψ) = S(Aψ), S(iψ) = Jd S(ψ), S(φ)^T S(ψ) = Re<φ|ψ>, S(φ)^T Jd S(ψ) = −Im<φ|ψ>, S(ψ)^T T(A) S(ψ) = Re<ψ|A|ψ>.
edges.scope: instances: d = 2, 3 (each identity is real-bilinear; the expansion is the same for every d)
edges.check: symbolic identities with real symbols for all components, d = 2, 3: all hold

edges.statement: T1(ρ) = T(ρ)/2 has unit trace, tr[T1(ρ)T(A)] = Re tr(ρA), and A ≥ 0 ⇒ T(A) ≥ 0.
edges.scope: instances: d = 2 (consequences of the d-independent identities of RQ1)
edges.check: trace and positivity identities, symbolic 2x2: all hold

edges.statement: P = (1 − J⊗J)/2 is the orthogonal projector onto span{ψ_even^(2), ψ_odd^(2)}; its kernel is spanned by |00>+|11>, |01>−|10>; on its range J⊗1 = 1⊗J.
edges.check: exact 4x4 computation on the two flags: all hold

edges.statement: S(ψ)⊗_F S(φ) = R(ψ⊗φ): the class of S(ψ)⊗S(φ) has canonical representative R(ψ⊗φ)/√2, and Eq. (34) is R(ψ⊗φ).
ψ_even^(N) + iψ_odd^(N) = 2^{−(N−1)/2}(|0>+i|1>)^{⊗N}; J_k ψ_even = ψ_odd and J_k ψ_odd = −ψ_even for every flag k; the subspace on which all J_k agree is two-dimensional.
edges.scope: instances: N = 1..6 (the product form makes the J_k statement immediate for every N)
edges.check: integer arithmetic, N = 1..6 flags (common-subspace dimension for N = 2..5): all hold

edges.statement: I^(N) is a projector, (J^(N))² = −I^(N); I^(N+M) = (I^(N)⊗I^(M) − J^(N)⊗J^(M))/2, J^(N+M) = (I^(N)⊗J^(M) + J^(N)⊗I^(M))/2; partial traces of I^(N), J^(N) are I^(N−M), J^(N−M).
edges.check: exact rational matrices, N up to 5: all hold

edges.statement: (T(A)⊗1)R(Ψ) = R((A⊗1)Ψ) and (1⊗T(B))R(Ψ) = R((1⊗B)Ψ) for all A, B and all Ψ ∈ C^dA⊗C^dB.
edges.check: 880 exact checks on real bases of operators and of C^dA (x) C^dB: (T(A) (x) 1) R(Psi) = R((A (x) 1) Psi) and the same on the B side, all hold

edges.statement: T(A)⊗T(B) commutes with P and P(T(A)⊗T(B)) = Re(A⊗B)⊗I^(2) + Im(A⊗B)⊗J^(2) = ½[T(A)⊗T(B) − T(iA)⊗T(iB)].
edges.scope: instances: dA = dB = 2 (bilinear in A and B)
edges.check: 64 operator pairs (real basis of M_2(C) x M_2(C)): [P, T(A)(x)T(B)] = 0, P (T(A)(x)T(B)) = Re(A(x)B)(x)I^(2) + Im(A(x)B)(x)J^(2), and this equals (1/2)[T(A)(x)T(B) - T(iA)(x)T(iB)]: all hold

edges.statement: R(Φ)^T [T(A)⊗T(B)] R(Ψ) = Re<Φ|A⊗B|Ψ>; hence all bipartite Born probabilities coincide with those of complex QT, entangled states included.
edges.check: 16384 exact checks (real bases of A, B, Phi, Psi; d = 2 each): the real bilinear form equals Re<Phi|A(x)B|Psi>

edges.statement: Complex QT with |φ+>_{AB1}|φ+>_{B2C}, A = (Z, X, Y), C = ((X±Z), (Y±Z), (X±Y))/√2 and Bob's Bell measurement gives P(b) = 1/4 and T = 6√2.
The real model with state |φ+>|φ+>|ψ_even^(4)> and operators T(Π^A)⊗T(Π^B)⊗T(Π^C) gives the same probabilities P(a,b,c|x,z) as complex QT for all outcomes and settings, hence T = 6√2.
edges.check: 112 moments <Π_b>, <A_x Π_b>, <Π_b C_z>, <A_x Π_b C_z> (they fix all 288 probabilities P(a,b,c|x,z)) agree exactly with complex QM; state, operators and values contain no imaginary part; T = 6*√2

edges.statement: The value 6√2 is obtained with the functional of Renou et al.; the form printed in the arXiv text (Eqs. (104)–(106), as extracted) differs in one sign prefactor and in the weighting.
edges.where: Eqs. (104)–(106) vs Renou et al. Supplementary
edges.check: T = 6√2 only with the prefactor (-1)^{b1} on (S_25 + S_26) and with either (joint correlators, plain sum over b) or (conditional correlators, P(b) weights); with (-1)^{b2} the outcomes b = 01, 10 give 4√2·P(b) and T = 5√2; joint correlators with an additional P(b) weight give 5√2/4

edges.statement: After Bob's outcome 00 the real Alice–Charlie state is |φ+><φ+|_AC ⊗ ½(|φ−><φ−| + |ψ+><ψ+|)_{A'C'}.
edges.check: exact: P(00) = 1/4 and the normalised Alice-Charlie state equals |φ+><φ+|_AC ⊗ (1/2)(|φ-><φ-| + |ψ+><ψ+|)_{A'C'}; the flag factor is I^(2)/2

edges.statement: The composite space has real dimension 2·dA·dB, not (2dA)(2dB), and the canonical state of two independent sources, ψ_even^(4) on flags (A'B1')(B2'C'), has Schmidt rank 2 across the source cut: the model does not satisfy postulate (iv) with product states for independent sources.
edges.where: main text (the tensor extension fails); Remark 5, Eq. (49); Sec. H
edges.check: exact: the composite space of two qubits has real dimension 8 = 2·dA·dB, not 16 = (2dA)(2dB); ψ_even^(4) = (ψ_even^(2)⊗ψ_even^(2) − ψ_odd^(2)⊗ψ_odd^(2))/√2 has Schmidt rank 2 across (A'B1')|(B2'C'); the product ψ_even^(2)⊗ψ_even^(2) projects onto ψ_even^(4)/√2

edges.statement: dim SY_n = n² = dim Herm_n and (nm)² = n²m²: the flag composition is locally tomographic; the real tensor product on symmetric matrices is not (excess nm(n−1)(m−1)/4).
edges.check: symbolic in n, m: the flag composition is locally tomographic on SY (same count as complex QT); the real tensor product on Sym has nm(n−1)(m−1)/4 extra parameters, > 0 for n, m ≥ 2

edges.statement: Real QM with postulate (iv) and independent real sources obeys T ≤ 7.6605.
edges.where: Ref. [12] (Renou et al.): cited in the introduction; bound 7.6605 quoted in Sec. H
edges.note: Bound from a semidefinite relaxation (NPA-type hierarchy); Renou et al. state that its tightness is open. Not re-derived here.

edges.statement: T(−iH) = −Jd T(H): the generator of the orthogonal group T(e^{−iHt}) is −Jd times the observable T(H).
edges.where: Props. 6, 7 (+ edge GN7 of the network)
edges.check: T(−iH) = −Jd T(H) (d symbolic); for Hermitian H the generator −Jd T(H) is antisymmetric and the observable T(H) symmetric (d = 2 explicit)

edges.statement: The real model and complex QT are isomorphic as theories (states, effects, composition, probabilities), so no experiment discriminates them.
edges.where: abstract; closing paragraph of the main text
edges.check: RQ1–RQ3 (single systems), RQ5–RQ9 (composition and local action) and RQ10 (Born rule on composites) give a bijection of states and observables that preserves every probability

edges.statement: RQ12 (T = 6√2 in the flag model) does not contradict RQ17 (T ≤ 7.6605): the premise 'postulate (iv)' of RQ17 fails for the flag model (RQ15).
edges.where: closing paragraph of the main text; Sec. H, last sentence
edges.check: scope separation: no-go RQ17 needs premise ax-tensorR; possibility RQ12 does not use it; RQ15 certifies its absence

edges.statement: 'The use of complex numbers is a matter of convenience.'
edges.note: RQ18 shows that the model contains the complex structure as the real operator J and RQ19 that it is complex QT in real coordinates. Whether that makes complex numbers 'a convenience' depends on what one counts as the theory; no edge decides it.

operations.why: the composition postulate is the premise that the 2025–26 papers change; it must be a node of its own so that edges D6 and F5 can name it
realification is a change of representation, not a model

RQ19: same states, effects, composition and probabilities; if model nodes are identified as GPTs up to linear isomorphism (the layer is described as 'concrete GPTs'), this is one node with two representations
edge D6 currently targets e-bell; the theorem of Renou et al. concerns the network functional T, not Bell nonlocality
states the premises under which the no-go holds (RQ17) and survives RQ12

operations.note: 'In real QM the generator is not an observable without superselection' — the flag model is exactly the superselection case: observables commute with J (RQ1, RQ18)
definition in terms of a complex structure J rather than of the number field, since RQ18 realises it over R
